Good but makes me uneasy. There are several things I genuinely like about it. I think the concept is creative, I like that the lamb grows as you spend time in Scripture, I like the ability to invite friends and the option for devotionals.

However, there are also some aspects that made me uncomfortable and caused me to question whether I could recommend this app to others.

The comments made by the lamb feel inappropriate at times. Being called “master,” along with phrases like “Even lambs rest, master,” or “Don’t worry, master, I notice every little thing you do,” feels strange and unnecessary.

There are also a few theological concerns. After completing a lesson, I received a message suggesting that my actions made angels happy. While I understand the intent, this didn’t feel biblically grounded and the way it was presented and made me uncomfortable.

When I asked the chatbot about this and it referenced Luke 15:10, but it pulled the verse out of context which is a major problem for Christians trying to understand the Bible

Overall, I think the idea behind this app is strong and there are features I really appreciate. However, due to these concerns, I’m not sure I can recommend it with a clear conscience at this point.

Serious Gospel Clarity Issues (Read Carefully). This app is well designed, engaging, and motivating, and I understand why it has so many positive reviews. However, after carefully testing the Bible Chat with clear, direct questions about salvation, I found serious and repeated doctrinal inconsistencies that cannot be ignored.

While the app often affirms salvation by grace through faith, it also blurs the biblical distinction between justification and works. On key gospel questions (repentance, good works, assurance of salvation), the AI gives conflicting answers, sometimes affirming faith alone and other times implying that works, obedience, or “evidence” are necessary to validate salvation.

This is not a minor theological difference. Scripture is clear:

“By grace you have been saved through faith… not of works.” (Ephesians 2:8 9)
“To him who does not work but believes… his faith is counted as righteousness.” (Romans 4:5)

Any Bible app especially one used by new believers… must be extremely careful not to introduce confusion about the gospel. Teaching that faith must later be proven by works undermines assurance and shifts trust away from Christ’s finished work and back onto human performance.

This app is emotionally engaging and popular, but popularity does not equal doctrinal accuracy (Matthew 7:13 14). I strongly urge users to test everything against Scripture and not rely on the AI for clear teaching on salvation.

Until the gospel is presented consistently, clearly, and without contradiction, I cannot recommend this app as a trustworthy Bible study tool.

“A little leaven leavens the whole lump.” (Galatians 5:9)
